comparison.text: The most polluted city on Earth in the 2025 IQAir report is Loni, in Delhi NCR: 112.5 ug/m3 average, 22x the WHO limit. All 25 worst cities were in India, Pakistan and China.
comparison.source_name: IQAir, 2025 World Air Quality Report press release
comparison.caveat: IQAir rankings blend government and low-cost sensor data and only cover cities that measure at all. Plenty of unmonitored places never make the list.

comparison.text: Mumbai today is 3x the air of Pune, the cleanest city we track. Same country, different lungs.
comparison.caveat: Same-day comparison across the five tracked cities using the same measurement rule for each. Only shown when the ratio is at least 1.5.

comparison.text: Official Indian AQI: 49 out of 500, category 'Good'. That is the government's own scale.
comparison.source_name: CPCB, National Air Quality Index (PM2.5 breakpoints)
comparison.caveat: Computed from PM2.5 alone. The full CPCB AQI takes the worst sub-index across pollutants, so the official city AQI can be higher on days another pollutant dominates.

comparison.text: A week of air like this = 9 cigarettes. Your lungs are keeping the receipts.
comparison.source_name: Berkeley Earth, Air Pollution and Cigarette Equivalence
comparison.caveat: Extends the Berkeley Earth per-day rule of thumb across a week at the same level. Real weeks vary day to day.

comparison.text: That is 1.3x the WHO daily safe limit. The limit is 15. We are not close.
comparison.source_name: WHO, 2021 Global Air Quality Guidelines (PM2.5 24-hour average 15 ug/m3)
comparison.caveat: WHO guidelines are health-based targets, not legal limits. India's own national standard (60 ug/m3 for 24h PM2.5) is four times looser.
